summary: The Device That Never Needed a Battery is an educational project about the Apollo 11 Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector. The project explains how this device, left on the Moon in 1969, works without a battery by reflecting laser pulses sent from Earth. It helps students understand its scientific importance and how NASA uses lunar laser ranging data to study the Earth-Moon system.
details: Our project focuses on the Apollo 11 Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector, a scientific instrument placed on the Moon during the Apollo 11 mission. Unlike many electronic devices, the retroreflector does not need a battery or an external power source. It works by reflecting laser pulses sent from Earth back toward their source. The project explains the idea behind lunar laser ranging and shows how scientists can use the return time of the laser signal to calculate the distance between Earth and the Moon. We used NASA resources and lunar laser ranging information to explain the device, its design, and its scientific importance. Our project presents this scientific concept in a simple and educational way so that students and space enthusiasts can understand how a relatively simple device can provide valuable scientific data for decades.
